newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Parana state sees booming investment.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Parana state sees booming investment.

text.p: Investment is booming in Brazil's Parana state as its infrastructure, quality of life and proximity to neighboring nations of the Mercosur trade group attract newcomers and encourage firms to expand.
In the last two years, the southern state drew about $5.5 billion in investment, of which 25 percent came from automakers, said Parana state Governor Jaime Lerner.

"In two years, we saw $5.5 billion in investment. This represents more jobs, more technology. Parana is becoming the major link to the Mercosur region," said Lerner, referring to the group made up of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
With 8.9 million people, Parana state represents the fifth largest state economy in the country after the states of Sao Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Rio Grande do Sul.
Parana accounted for 6.25 percent of Brazil's gross domestic product in 1994, with a GDP per capita of $3,824.
Lerner said better quality of life, Parana's strategic location, transportation and telecommunications infrastructure and skilled labor pool have contributed to lure new investment.
But a tax incentives program has also been behind the companies' decision to come or expand activities in the state.
Parana state has launched a program called "Parana Mais Empregos" (Parana More Jobs), which offers a 49-month grace period before they start paying the so-called ICMS tax.

The last foreign firm to decide to invest in the Parana was U.S. carmaker Chrysler Corporation which on Thursday signed a deal to set up a $315 million Dakota pick-up truck plant in Campo Largo, 30 km from Curitiba.

The carmaker will begin next month to build the plant which will initially produce 12,000 units a year and create 400 direct jobs. Production is expected to start at the end of the second quarter of 1998.

France's Renault kicked off the automakers' investment wave in Parana state and is investing $1.0 billion in a plant in Sao Jose dos Pinhais to make 30,000 vehicles a year as of 1998. Output is expected to grow to 120,000 units in the following year.

Other investment plans announced by foreign car and auto part manufacturers include Volkswagen -Audi's $500 million plant to make vehicles as of December 1998 and Detroit Diesel Corporation's 40 million real investment in a motor plant, the state government said in a statement.

Local meat processors Sadia and Dagranja, beer maker Kaiser, Portugal's Tafisa group, Swedish appliance manufacturer Electrolux Brazil unit and pulp maker Iberia are some other companies that are investing in the state, it added.
According to a survey by Parana state's Industry and Commerce Secretariat, 220 companies showed interest in opening business in the state last year.
